'''Johannes Geiss''' (4 September 1926 – 30 January 2020) was a [[German people|German]] physicist.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lematin.ch/sante/sciences/createur-experience-suisse-dapollo-11-decede/story/13001763|title=Espace: Le créateur de l'expérience suisse d'Apollo 11 est décédé|date=5 February 2020|work=lematin.ch|language=French|access-date=6 February 2020|archive-date=4 February 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200204154104/https://www.lematin.ch/sante/sciences/createur-experience-suisse-dapollo-11-decede/story/13001763|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Biography==
Geiss was born in 1926 in modern-day [[Poland]], the son of farmers Hans Geiss and Irene Wilk. In 1955, he married Carmen Bach.

Geiss studied physics in [[Göttingen]] from 1947 to 1950. He published his doctoral thesis in 1953, titled ''Isotopenanalysen an „gewöhnlichem Blei“''. He then conducted research on [[geochronology]] at the [[University of Bern]] and [[University of Chicago]]. From 1958 to 1959, Geiss was an associate professor at the [[University of Miami]] before returning to [[Bern]], working there until 1991. At Bern he devised the [[Solar Wind Composition Experiment]] for the [[Apollo program]] to measure the isotopic and elemental composition of noble gases in the [[solar wind]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=First 'flag' on the Moon? |url=https://www.esa.int/About_Us/ESA_history/First_flag_on_the_Moon |access-date=2024-09-20 |website=www.esa.int |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Solar Wind Composition Experiment |url=https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/experiment/display.action?id=1971-008C-03 |website=nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov}}</ref> From 1995 to 2002, he was co-director of the [[International Space Science Institute]]. In 2019, a bronze statue of Geiss was erected on the University of Bern campus by Horst Bohnet.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/first-moon-landing_the-beautiful-lunar-toy-from-bern--/45103206|title=The beautiful lunar toy from Bern|date=19 July 2019|work=swissinfo.ch}}</ref>

Johannes Geiss died on 30 January 2020 at the age of 93.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nzz.ch/wissenschaft/johannes-geiss-der-physiker-mit-dem-sonnenwindsegel-ist-tot-ld.1538396|title=Der Mann mit dem Sonnenwindsegel auf dem Mond: Johannes Geiss, Pionier der Weltraumforschung, ist tot|date=4 February 2020|work=Neue Zürcher Zeitung|language=German |last1=Feusi |first1=Alois }}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
*Honorary Member of the [[French Academy of Sciences]] (1978)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/johannes-geiss-g3lcya/|title=Johannes Geiss|work=National Academy of Sciences|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170808233127/http://www.nasonline.org/member-directory/members/46651.html|archive-date=8 August 2017}}</ref>
*Honorary Member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (1978)
*[[Allan D. Emil Memorial Award]] (1989)
*Honorary Member of the [[Academia Europaea]] (1989)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Geiss_Johannes|title=Johannes Geiss|work=Academia Europaea}}</ref>
*[[Albert Einstein Medal]] (2001)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.einstein-bern.ch/index.php?lang=de&show=laudatio&subs=geiss|title=Verleihung der Albert Einstein Medaille 2001|date=13 August 2003|work=Einsteinhaus Bern|language=German}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/astrophysicist-receives-albert-einstein-medal/2074846|title=Astrophysicist receives Albert Einstein medal|date=11 June 2001|work=swissinfo.ch}}</ref>
*[[William Bowie Medal]] (2005)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://honors.agu.org/winners/johannes-geiss/|title=Johannes Geiss - Honors Program|work=American Geophysical Union}}</ref>
